shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index rose to a one-week high on Tuesday, helped by stronger rates across all vessel segments.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index rose to a one-week high on Tuesday, helped by stronger rates across all vessel segments.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, rose 33 points, or ~1%, to 3,432 points, highest since September 14.
The capesize index (.BACI) rose 53 points, or 0.9%, to 5,892 points.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes including iron ore and coal, increased by $488 to $49,938.
However, iron ore futures fell, snapping a four-day gaining streak, as a weak near-term demand outlook weighed on the market and a stronger yuan added more pressure on the yuan-denominated contract.
The panamax index (.BPNI) rose 44 points, or 1.9%, to 2,299 points.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, gained $390 to $20,687.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) inched up 5 points, or 0.3%, to 1,776.
